scores/scores: A classifier hands back one score per class. Here there are three: two, one, and minus one.
scores/want: Often we want probabilities instead. Every one positive, and all of them adding up to one.
scores/fail: These scores fail both tests. Minus one is negative, and together they add up to two.
exp/two: Softmax fixes both in two moves.
exp/exp: First, raise e, about two point seven one eight, to the power of each score.
exp/pos: e to any power is positive, so minus one becomes zero point three seven.
exp/grow: And each extra point of score multiplies by about two point seven, so the top score pulls ahead: two becomes seven point three nine.
divide/total: Second, add them up. The total is ten point four eight.
divide/divide: Then divide each one by that total.
divide/result: Class zero gets zero point seven one, class one zero point two six, and class two zero point zero four.
divide/check: All positive, and they add up to one.
divide/formula: In symbols: p k is e to the s k, divided by the sum of e to the s j, over every class j.
gaps/shift: Add five to every score. Every exponential gets multiplied by the same factor, and that factor cancels when we divide. Nothing changes.
gaps/scale: Double every score instead, and the gaps between them double. The top class grows to zero point eight eight.
gaps/soft: That is the name: a soft maximum. The top score gets most of the probability, but every class keeps a little.
example/ask: Your turn. The scores are one, zero and two. What probability does class two get?
example/e: Exponentiate: two point seven two, one, and seven point three nine.
example/sum: Add them: eleven point one one.
example/p: Divide class two's by the total: seven point three nine over eleven point one one is about zero point six seven.
